newsitem.title: USA: NY precious metals end mixed in light trade.
newsitem.headline: NY precious metals end mixed in light trade.

text.p: New York precious metals futures ended mixed Friday, on light volumes, with direction still unclear, after giving back the week's gains on Thursday.
"Gold has stabilized above support at $380 an ounce, basis December, and could begin to garner support from several fronts," Prudential Securities analyst Bette Raptopoulos said.
"We favor the long side as we expect an expansionary global economy, related inflationary concerns and a reallocation of assets by hedge funds and individual investors (out of equities)," she said.
COMEX December gold ended down 30 cents at $384.60 an ounce, after trading in a $384.90-$383.90 range, with estimate gold futures volume moderate at 16,000 lots.
The latest CFTC Commitment of Traders data, due late Friday, and the OTC options expiry Tuesday may provide more direction, traders said.
In bullion trade, spot gold ended quoted $382.55/383.05, compared to the London Friday afternoon fix at $382.55 and the New York close Thursday at $382.85/383.25.

Historical volatility in gold has fallen to the lowest levels since 1980 and the assumption is that nothing will move the gold market, while the Swiss franc continues to soar, ahead of the creation of Europe's single currency, Grant's Interest Rate Observer editor, James Grant, noted Friday.

"To draw an inference from the recent complacent market action, the Swiss National Bank will never lose the confidence of the world's savings constituency, while the gold market will never regain it," Grant said.
"However, we think Mr Market is serving up the kind of extreme valuations that sometimes precede profitable speculations."
"If we read the signs right, one should short (Swiss) francs, and go long gold," he said.
COMEX December silver closed up 0.7 cent at $4.925 an ounce, after trading in a $4.940-4.900 range.
Earlier this week both silver and gold recovered to two week highs, but the longer term six week downtrend has not yet been convincingly reversed, analysts said.
NYMEX January platinum settled down $1.90 at $388.10, while NYMEX December palladium closed down 65 cents at $118.25.

"In recent months Russia's need for hard currency has been the dominant production consideration (for platinum and palladium)," Raptopoulos said. "As a result stockpiled metal came onto the market and pressured prices."
--Clive Mckeef, New York Commodities 212-859-1641; email: clive.mckeef@reuters.com
